info.name: Kairox Automation
info.description: Automation (kx.automation): channel webhooks, the unsubscribe page, channels admin. Generated by scripts/gen_handoff.py from the code; read docs/handoff/CRM_API.md (channels admin) and README.md. Pick the Kairox local or staging environment. Sign in once (folder 01); the collection then renews the staff token by itself.

request.description:
End this session: the refresh token (cookie) and the session the access token names are revoked and the cookie cleared.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

Recovery: a code to the work address. Always 202 (nobody learns which addresses exist); 429 when the rate limit for this IP or this typed address is reached (the same for unknown addresses, M3). L6: the code is mailed after the response, so a real address answers as fast as an unknown one.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 202

Recovery step 2: the emailed code + a new password (min 12 characters); every session ends.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

item.name: 08 Channels admin
item.description: Company WhatsApp numbers / mailboxes and message templates.

request.description:
§20.11 company WhatsApp numbers and email addresses, with the countries each number serves.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Regional routing for WhatsApp numbers: which countries a number serves, the default number.

**Who may call it:** admin + signed in with the authenticator app (mfa=true)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

§20.11 message templates and Meta's approval state, every version (the history), newest first; `live` marks the version being sent. `current_only=true`: the newest version of each template.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Add or change a template. Editing the live (approved) WhatsApp version creates a NEW version that waits for Meta under its own name; the approved one keeps sending until Meta approves the new one. A version not yet approved (draft, submitted, rejected) is changed in place. Email templates go live at once (no provider approval); the previous email version is kept as history.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin + signed in with the authenticator app (mfa=true)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

item.name: 09 Buyer simulation - WhatsApp
item.description: Pretend to be a buyer on WhatsApp. The request is signed automatically from wa_app_secret.

request.description:
Whatsapp Events

**Who may call it:** Meta (WhatsApp Cloud API): header X-Hub-Signature-256 = HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the app secret

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

**How to use:** set `buyer_phone` (digits only, e.g. 971501234567), `buyer_name` and `buyer_text` (the buyer's words), then Send. The pre-request script builds a fresh message id and timestamp and signs the body. The answer is always an empty 200 (Meta needs it fast); the AI reply arrives a few seconds later: run 'List deals' then 'Deal timeline'. To test duplicate delivery, set `wa_reuse_last_id` = yes.

exec: // Builds a fresh WhatsApp Cloud API webhook (new message id + timestamp) and signs it the way Meta does:
if (!secret) { throw new Error("wa_app_secret is empty in the environment: ask the admin (staging) or use the local environment file."); }
const msgId = reuse ? pm.environment.get("last_wa_message_id") : "wamid.QA" + Date.now() + Math.floor(Math.random() * 1e6);
contacts: [{ wa_id: pm.variables.get("buyer_phone"), profile: { name: pm.variables.get("buyer_name") } }],
messages: [{ from: pm.variables.get("buyer_phone"), id: msgId, timestamp: String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)),

request.description:
Whatsapp Verify

**Who may call it:** Meta (WhatsApp Cloud API): header X-Hub-Signature-256 = HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the app secret

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

item.name: 11 CMS publish webhook
item.description: Pretend to be the website CMS publishing a product. Signed automatically.

request.description:
Cms Published

**Who may call it:** The website CMS: headers X-Kx-Timestamp + X-Kx-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 of '<timestamp>.<body>'), max 5 minutes old

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

**How to use:** set `cms_product_code` to a product code (SKU) that exists in the CRM and `cms_operation` to publish or unpublish. The spec deliberately contains `price_aed`: the platform must drop it (prices never come from the CMS).

exec: // Signs like the CMS: X-Kx-Timestamp = unix seconds, X-Kx-Signature = sha256=<HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + '.' + body)>.
if (!secret) { throw new Error("cms_webhook_secret is empty in the environment: ask the admin / developer."); }
product: { code: pm.variables.get("cms_product_code"), name: "Aluminium container 750 ml (QA test)",
spec: { material: "aluminium", capacity_ml: 750, price_aed: 1.23 }, custom_printing: false }

item.description: The one-click unsubscribe link printed in every buyer email.

request.description:
The page behind the link: one button, an optional reason (a GET changes nothing).

**Who may call it:** The buyer (anyone holding the signed link from an email)

**How to use:** copy the `t=` value from the unsubscribe link in a buyer email into `unsubscribe_token`. A GET must NEVER unsubscribe (mail scanners open links).

Stops every channel at once (§8.1 step 2) and records the optional reason (step 4).

**How to use:** copy the `t=` value from the unsubscribe link in a buyer email into `unsubscribe_token`.

item.name: 13 Telnyx call webhooks
item.description: Call-status callbacks from the phone provider. Signed automatically (URL token).

item.name: Alert call - staff pressed a key (signed URL)

request.description:
Telnyx Gather

**Who may call it:** Telnyx: signed per-call URL token ?t=... (plus an Ed25519 signature header when the Telnyx public key is configured)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

**How to use:** `attempt_id` is saved by 'Click-to-call' (folder 03) or given by the developer. The URL token is computed from `telnyx_callback_secret`.

exec: // The per-call URL token the platform puts in Telnyx callback URLs: base64url(JSON claims) + '.' + hex HMAC-SHA256.
if (!secret) { throw new Error("telnyx_callback_secret is empty in the environment: ask the admin / developer."); }
const claims = JSON.stringify({ a: pm.environment.get("attempt_id"), exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600 });

request.description:
Signed with the wrong secret. Nothing may be stored (check: no new deal / timeline entry).

request.description:
No ?t= token (or a random attempt id). Postman cannot make Telnyx's Ed25519 signature, so this negative test is the check for the signature path.

**Expected:** HTTP 401, 404, 422
